inyoite.identity: IMA September 2026 PDF p.102: CaB3O3(OH)5(H2O)3·H2O, grandfathered G, original year 1914; year is not a sequential approval ID. Historical natural occurrence in Schaller 1916 pp.35–40, Mount Blanco, Death Valley. The 0.1037-g analysis did not measure boron; B2O3 was calculated by difference.
inyoite.experiment: Comboni 2022 accepted manuscript pp.3–9, all five figures/tables and official supplements inspected. One museum crystal approximately 20×15×10 micrometres, unreported collection locality/chemical assay, helium DAC at ESRF ID15B, ruby uncertainty 0.05 GPa; deposited models approximately 293 K. The 8.25(5) to 8.86(5) GPa sampled interval contains the transition. Table1 volumes824.75(6) to762(2) Å³ imply about7.6% drop across steps, not an equilibrium threshold.
limits: High-pressure structure unsolved; metrically monoclinic with P21/n suggested by extinctions. Boron III-to-IV coordination is hypothesized by analogy, not observed in a solved high-pressure model. Hydrogen positions not refined.
No reflections were found on ambient decompression despite repeated attempts. This is not proof of reversible crystallinity, a quantified amorphous fraction, recovery yield or industrial use.
Abstract19.80(5) GPa conflicts with Table1 maximum18.91(5) and body18.9; no silently repaired maximum. Table1 at2.00 GPa prints944.0(1)Å³, matching CIF923.96(11); geometry independently gives923.958.

Twelve official CIFs contain16 non-H sites each and cover the starting phase through8.25 GPa only; no high-pressure structure. CIF comment/field differences are not normalized: file10 comment7.23 versus cell matching TableS1 5.19; files3/4 comments0.33/0.82 vsS1 0.34/0.81 within stated0.05 uncertainty. File13 lacks pressure field but comment8.25.

Fig3 caption plane label versus plotted label differs; no specific-plane extinction claim adopted. TableS1 distinguishes total and unique reflections whereas main text labels1658 observed; no disputed count adopted.

Schaller1916 MountBlanco occurrence differs from the 2022 introduction attributing Kramer locality to Schaller. Neither establishes provenance of the modern museum specimen. Historical inyoite-to-meyerhofferite alteration is inferred from textures, not the pressure experiment.
